chunks.subject: AP World History
chunks.title: LEQ — Long Essay Question (6 points) — Q2 Set 1: Belief Systems and Societies in Asia
chunks.content: AP World History LEQ, 6 points, standardized rubric (Q2/Q3/Q4 are period options; students choose one). A Thesis/Claim [1]: defensible thesis with a line of reasoning. B Contextualization [1]: broader relevant context. C Evidence [0–2]: (1) at least two specific relevant pieces of evidence; (1) evidence used to support the argument. D Analysis and Reasoning [0–2]: (1) a reasoning process (comparison, causation, or continuity/change) frames the argument; (1) demonstrates a complex understanding. Q2 Set 1 prompt: belief systems and societies in Asia. Common failure: brief/absent contextualization; evidence listed but not used; reasoning process without complexity.

chunks.subject: AP World History
chunks.title: LEQ Q2 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2A, 6/6
chunks.content: Q2 (Set 1) scored 6/6 (Thesis 1, Context 1, Evidence 2, Analysis 2). Defensible thesis, contextualization, two used pieces of evidence, and both reasoning points (a reasoning process plus complex understanding). Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP World History
chunks.title: LEQ Q2 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2B, 4/6
chunks.content: Q2 (Set 1) scored 4/6 (Thesis 1, Context 0, Evidence 2, Analysis 1). Earned the thesis, both Evidence points, and one Analysis point (reasoning process). Lost Contextualization and the Complexity point. A common 4-point profile: strong thesis/evidence, weak context, no complexity.

chunks.subject: AP World History
chunks.title: LEQ Q2 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2C, 1/6
chunks.content: Q2 (Set 1) scored 1/6 (Thesis 1, Context 0, Evidence 0, Analysis 0). Earned only the thesis. Lost contextualization, both Evidence points (no specific, used evidence), and both Analysis points. Illustrates a claim with no substantiation.
